job.title: Workers Compensation Team Leader
job.description:
Our client is one of the most significant private-sector employers in the country, supporting team members nationally.

About the opportunity
This is a rare opportunity to step into a pivotal leadership role within a business genuinely committed to Human-Centric Care, moving beyond compliance to deliver purpose-led outcomes that place people at the heart of their recovery journey.

Reporting directly to senior leadership within the Workers Compensation function, you will lead and support a team responsible for driving consistent, high-quality claims outcomes across a complex self-insurance portfolio, while working closely with a third-party administrator.

About you
You are a subject-matter expert in VIC Workers Compensation with proven leadership experience gained within a self-insured organisation. You bring strong interpretation and application of workers' compensation legislation and regulations, and you're ready to hit the ground running in a fast-paced remediation and stabilisation program.

Responsibilities and Duties
  • Lead, coach, and support a team of Case Managers to ensure accurate, timely, and compliant claims decisions
  • Provide expert technical guidance on complex and challenging claims
  • Promote consistency and quality in claims decision-making through regular case reviews and team oversight
  • Monitor and drive delivery of remediation plans to improve claims management compliance
  • Maintain comprehensive, accurate documentation to support decision-making and audit readiness
  • Champion a customer-focused culture across the team, ensuring injured workers and employers are treated with empathy, respect, and transparency
  • Oversee resolution of escalated queries, complaints, and disputes, ensuring timely and appropriate outcomes
  • Ensure strict team-wide compliance with workers' compensation legislation, self-insurance requirements, and organisational policy
  • Maintain up-to-date knowledge of relevant legislative and regulatory changes and cascade this to the team
  • Identify potential risks within claims and lead mitigation strategies
  • Support audits and quality assurance reviews of processes and systems of work
  • Foster a positive, supportive team culture built on open communication, shared learning, and collective accountability
  • Develop and deliver training and coaching to ensure the team is well-versed in current legislation and best practice across claims management, customer service, and compliance
Required Skills and Experience
  • Essential: Previous experience working within a self-insured organisation
  • Minimum 5 years' experience in workers' compensation case management, with demonstrated people leadership or team leader experience
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret complex information and provide clear, evidence-based guidance
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence and engage across all levels
  • Strong leadership, coaching, and mentoring capability
  • Sound IT literacy across Microsoft and Google ecosystems, with exposure to multiple claims systems and reporting platforms
  • Demonstrated experience managing complex claims and interpreting relevant legislation and regulatory frameworks.
How to apply 
For more information, please apply directly via the link with your resume. For additional inquiries, contact Jo Retallick at 0482 076 255 

Thank you for your interest, we look forward to receiving your application!

job.title: Rail Safety Professionals - Advisors to Managers
job.description:

We partner with leading contractors, asset owners, operators and consultancies delivering some of Australia's most significant rail, transport and infrastructure programs.

We are interested in speaking with professionals across all levels, including:

  • Senior Safety Advisors
  • Rail Safety Specialists
  • Safety Assurance Professionals

Opportunities will range from site-based project delivery roles through to corporate, governance and assurance positions, with both permanent and contract engagements available.

About the opportunities

Depending on your experience and the position, responsibilities may include:
  • Supporting the implementation of WHS and Rail Safety Management Systems
  • Providing practical safety advice to project teams, leadership and contractors
  • Managing and monitoring critical safety risks across rail and infrastructure environments
  • Conducting safety inspections, audits, surveillance and assurance activities
  • Supporting contractor safety management and compliance
  • Leading or supporting incident investigations and corrective actions
  • Supporting safe working and rail operational safety requirements
  • Participating in safety-in-design and risk assessment processes
  • Coaching and mentoring project teams to improve safety performance and culture
  • Ensuring compliance with relevant WHS legislation, rail safety legislation and project requirements
  • Supporting continuous improvement across safety systems, processes and performance
About you

We are interested in hearing from candidates with experience across rail construction, operations, maintenance, major infrastructure or transport projects.

Depending on the level of role, relevant qualifications and experience may include:
  • Certificate IV, Diploma or tertiary qualification in Work Health & Safety
  • Demonstrated experience within rail, transport or major infrastructure environments
  • Knowledge of WHS legislation and rail safety regulatory requirements
  • Understanding of Rail Safety Management Systems and assurance frameworks
  • Experience working with principal contractors, delivery partners, operators or asset owners
  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills
  • Experience in risk management, auditing, incident investigation and contractor management
  • Rail Industry Worker (RIW) competency and relevant rail/safe working qualifications will be highly regarded
Next steps

Apply with your current CV and a brief note on your background. Applications are reviewed as received.

job.title: Health & Safety Business Partner - 4 month contact
job.description:
A national leader in manufacturing and production is looking to bring an experienced Health & Safety Advisor onto their operations team. This is an initial 4-month engagement with genuine scope to extend for the right person.
You'll be based on-site, embedded within a fast-paced industrial operation, working directly alongside the people who run it day to day. It's a role for someone who's happiest out on the floor rather than behind a desk — someone who can earn trust quickly, spot risk before it becomes a problem, and help shift safety from a compliance checkbox to something the whole team actually owns.
 
Please note, travel across NSW will be required from time to time. 

What you'll be doing
  • Acting as the go-to safety resource for site leaders, supervisors, and frontline crews
  • Getting out on the floor for inspections, audits, and risk assessments
  • Leading investigations into incidents and near misses, and following through on corrective actions
  • Helping embed and strengthen the site's Safety Management System
  • Running inductions, toolbox talks, and on-the-job training
  • Keeping the site aligned with WHS legislation and internal standards
  • Managing safety documentation and reporting with accuracy and rigor
  • Overseeing contractor safety compliance and permit-to-work processes
What you'll bring
  • A WHS Diploma or Degree, or equivalent hands-on experience
  • Runs on the board as a Health & Safety Advisor in manufacturing, industrial, or heavy operations environments
  • Strong grasp of WHS legislation and how safety management systems work in practice
  • Real experience leading incident investigations and risk assessments, not just reviewing them
  • The communication skills to influence everyone from machine operators to senior leaders
  • Comfortable owning your patch independently, while staying connected to the wider HSE team
  • A current driver's licence
To be considered for the role please 'apply' by submitting an up to date word version of your CV. For a confidential conversation please contact Matt on 0480 004 970.

job.title: Emergency Management Trainer
job.description:
Our client is a large and complex public health service organisation in Melbourne’s western suburbs, providing a broad range of services to a diverse and growing population. With a significant workforce operating across multiple sites and a wide range of clinical and non-clinical environments, the organisation is committed to maintaining a safe, resilient and well-prepared workplace.

This is an opportunity to join an organisation where emergency preparedness, business continuity and employee safety are critical to maintaining essential services and protecting patients, visitors and staff.

The Role
We are seeking an experienced Emergency Management Officer to support the organisation’s emergency preparedness, response and recovery capability. This role will have a strong focus on evacuation planning, emergency response procedures, exercising and employee training, ensuring people are well prepared to respond effectively to a range of emergency scenarios.

Working closely with operational teams and key stakeholders, you will help build a strong emergency management culture by developing practical plans, delivering engaging training and testing organisational readiness through exercises and simulations.
Key Responsibilities
  • Develop, review and maintain emergency management and evacuation plans across the organisation.
  • Conduct site assessments and identify opportunities to strengthen emergency preparedness and evacuation capability.
  • Develop and deliver emergency management, evacuation and emergency response training to employees, including Wardens and key emergency response personnel.
  • Develop and facilitate emergency exercises, drills and simulations to test organisational readiness and identify areas for improvement.
  • Provide guidance and support to employees and leaders regarding emergency response procedures, evacuation requirements and emergency roles and responsibilities.
  • Support the development and maintenance of Business Continuity and Emergency Management programs.
  • Review emergency management documentation, procedures and processes to ensure they remain current, practical and fit for purpose.
  • Assess emergency management capability and provide reports and recommendations to address identified gaps.
  • Coordinate emergency response activities and provide support during incidents and exercises where required.
  • Work collaboratively with stakeholders to promote a positive emergency preparedness and safety culture.
  • Maintain awareness of relevant legislation, standards and contemporary emergency management practices.
Essential Experience & Criteria
  • Relevant experience in emergency management, emergency planning, business continuity, risk management or a related field.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and reviewing evacuation and emergency response plans.
  • Proven experience delivering emergency management and evacuation training to employees and/or emergency response teams.
  • Experience developing and facilitating emergency exercises, drills and simulations.
  • Strong understanding of emergency management principles, risk assessment and organisational preparedness.
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively across all levels of an organisation.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to develop clear plans, procedures, reports and training materials.
  • Ability to identify gaps in emergency preparedness and develop practical, achievable recommendations.
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in Emergency Management, Risk Management, Business Continuity, Occupational Health & Safety or a related discipline will be highly regarded.
What’s on Offer This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Emergency Management professional to play a key role in strengthening organisational preparedness, with a particular focus on evacuation planning, employee capability and emergency response training.

You will work with a broad range of stakeholders and have the opportunity to make a tangible impact on the organisation’s ability to prepare for and respond effectively to emergencies while supporting the delivery of essential community services.

How to apply 
For more information, please apply directly via the link with your resume. For additional inquiries, contact Jo Retallick at 0482 076 255 

Thank you for your interest, we look forward to receiving your application!

job.title: HSE System Improvement & Reporting
job.description:
THE COMPANY

This organisation owns and operates the high voltage transmission infrastructure that powers South Australia, sitting at the centre of one of the most renewables-intensive electricity systems in the world. With a capital works pipeline approaching $4 billion and projects currently reshaping how the state generates and moves energy, this is a business with genuine momentum behind it. The culture is collaborative, the engagement scores are high, and the people here consistently describe meaningful work and strong leadership. For someone who wants their contribution to matter, this is that kind of place.

THE ROLE

This is not a traditional safety role and it is not being advertised as one. This organisation has reached a point in its safety maturity where data, systems and governance are as important as boots on the ground, and they need someone who gets that.

The systems environment is well established and in good shape, but there is real work to do. Some areas are more manual than they should be, some reporting is more complex than it needs to be, and the narrative being delivered to leadership could be sharper. This person's job is to fix that, to own the data, govern it properly, and turn it into something the Board and Executive Management Team can actually act on.

If you have spent your HSE career gravitating toward the systems and data side of the profession, if you get frustrated when platforms do not talk to each other or when good data produces mediocre reporting, this role was written for you.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Lead the optimisation and integration of HSE management systems aligned to ISO 45001 and ISO 14001
  • Own HSE data governance frameworks including data ownership, quality, definitions and metrics
  • Collect, validate and analyse HSE and risk data across multiple systems to identify trends, anomalies and gaps
  • Translate complex HSE data into clear, compelling narratives for non-technical audiences including the Executive Management Team and Board
  • Deliver recurring reporting packs, trend analysis and critical control verification reporting for Divisional Leadership Teams
  • Champion automation and AI-enabled ways of working across the HSE function
  • Drive continuous improvement of reporting cadence, format and content in line with stakeholder needs
THE ESSENTIALS
  • Proven experience within HSE systems, analytics, digital improvement or related roles in high-risk industries
  • Demonstrated experience building or improving data governance frameworks and digital HSE workflows
  • Strong Power BI and Excel capability
  • Experience with HSE management systems such as SAP EHS, Intelex or equivalent
  • Solid understanding of HSE metrics including TRIFR, LTIFR, leading and lagging indicators and assurance models including ISO 45001, ISO 14001 and ISO 31000
  • Ability to prepare Board and executive level materials and communicate findings clearly to non-technical audiences
  • Background in construction, electrical, heavy industry, utilities or mining strongly preferred
THE BENEFITS
  • Five weeks annual leave
  • 16 weeks paid parental leave
  • Hybrid working, three days in the office and two from home with flexible start times
  • Pool vehicles for all site travel
  • Generous and achievable bonuses
  • Endorsed Work180 employer
NEXT STEPS

Apply with your current CV and a brief note on your background. Applications are reviewed as received. Alternatively, call direct for a confidential discussion.

James German | 0481 606 899 | james.german@zenergygroup.com.au

job.title: Environment Business Partner
job.description:
THE COMPANY

This is one of Australia's largest vertically integrated construction materials businesses, with operations spanning quarrying, cement, concrete, asphalt and recycling nationwide. It's the kind of organisation where the environmental function isn't an afterthought bolted onto operations, it sits inside a dedicated Property, Planning and Environment structure with real investment behind it. If you want to work somewhere your expertise actually shapes how a business runs day to day, not just ticks a compliance box, this is that kind of environment.

THE ROLE

This is an Environment Business Partner position, reporting into a Senior Environment Business Partner. It's a hands on specialist role rather than a people leadership one, there are no direct reports here, which means your time and expertise stay focused on the work itself rather than being pulled into managing a team.

The role exists to embed proactive, risk based environmental management across a genuinely broad operational footprint. You'll be working directly with site managers and operational leaders on the ground, not sitting removed from the action behind a desk. Based in Port Melbourne, the role covers operations across Victoria and Tasmania, giving you real breadth and variety in the sites and challenges you're working across week to week.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Own environmental permit verifications and impacts register reviews across a multi site portfolio, keeping everything current and defensible
  • Build real relationships with regulator contacts at both officer and senior level, not just reactive engagement when something goes wrong
  • Lead high potential incident investigations and validate action closeout, giving you genuine authority in how incidents are handled
  • Coach and upskill operational teams so environmental thinking becomes part of how sites operate, not something imposed from outside
  • Contribute to strategy and improvement plans for the region, with visibility into national direction and product line action plans
  • Stay connected to industry associations and circular economy thinking, keeping your expertise current and your network active
THE ESSENTIALS
  • Minimum 5 years environmental experience gained in heavy industry or with a regulator
  • Tertiary qualification in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Sustainability or related field
  • Solid working knowledge of environmental regulations and EPA licensing requirements
  • Comfortable holding your own in front of regional and operational management teams
  • A full driver's licence and genuine willingness to be on site regularly, this role covers real ground
THE BENEFITS
  • 14 weeks paid parental leave
  • Access to an Employee Assistance Program for you and your family, covering mental health and wellbeing support
  • Novated leasing options to package a vehicle through your pay
  • Employee discounts across everyday costs including groceries, energy, health and fitness, and retail
  • Genuine autonomy and trust to run your patch, not micromanagement
  • A realistic working structure, two days in the Port Melbourne office, two days on site, one day working from home
NEXT STEPS
Apply with your current CV and a brief note on your background. Applications are reviewed as received. Alternatively, call direct for a confidential discussion.

James German | 0481 606 899 | james.german@zenergygroup.com.au

job.title: Site HSE Manager
job.description:
Full Job Description

Zenergy is partnering with a leading organisation to appoint an experienced Site HSE Manager for a major data centre construction project in Sydney.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced safety professional to take a senior site-based role on a large-scale, technically complex construction project. Working closely with the project leadership team, contractors and subcontractors, you will be responsible for driving a strong safety culture and ensuring HSE standards are maintained throughout delivery.

About the role

As Site HSE Manager, you will lead HSE activities across the project, providing visible leadership on site and working closely with construction teams, contractors and key project stakeholders.

Key responsibilities will include:
  • Lead day-to-day HSE management across the project
  • Provide visible safety leadership across site activities
  • Manage and mentor site-based HSE personnel
  • Work closely with Project Managers, Construction Managers and subcontractors
  • Oversee contractor HSE performance and compliance
  • Review SWMS, risk assessments and high-risk construction activities
  • Conduct site inspections, audits and assurance activities
  • Monitor project HSE performance, trends and reporting
  • Ensure compliance with project HSE systems, Australian WHS legislation and client requirements
  • Support the development of a proactive and positive safety culture across the project
About You

We're looking for an experienced construction safety professional who can operate effectively within a large and fast-paced project environment.

Ideally, you will have:
  • 5+ years' experience within health and safety
  • Previous experience working for a Tier 1 or major construction contractor
  • Experience delivering large-scale construction or infrastructure projects, ideally valued at $400m+
  • Previous experience in a Site HSE Manager, Safety Manager, Senior HSE Advisor or similar senior site-based position
  • Data centre, mission-critical, major building or complex infrastructure experience highly regarded
  • Strong contractor and subcontractor management experience
  • Demonstrated ability to influence construction teams and senior project stakeholders
  • Strong knowledge of Australian WHS legislation and high-risk construction activities
  • Relevant tertiary or formal qualifications in WHS/OHS
  • Full Australian working rights
Why Zenergy?

Zenergy has been Australia's leading specialist HSEQ recruitment consultancy for the past 20 years, partnering with many of the country's most respected contractors, asset owners and principal organisations.

Our team has an extensive network across the construction and infrastructure sectors and is trusted to deliver HSEQ professionals across some of Australia's largest and most complex projects.
